title: Connect a Git repository
prompt:
Story 1: Connect a Git repository, on GitHub or GitLab, with an API key

- **Story**: XXX-connect-git-repository
- **Created**: 2026-11-07
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: in Integrations, choose GitHub or GitLab, paste a key and a repository, see "Connected" with the repository and who the key
  belongs to; change the provider; remove the key and see every Sync button say that nothing is connected.

## Story

As a team member, I want to choose GitHub or GitLab and connect my project to a repository there by pasting an API key in Integrations,
so that BWYN can keep the project's documents in the repository my team already uses, and my key never leaves the backend.

## Acceptance tests

The card and the choice of provider

- [ ] **Given** Integrations in a project with no connection, **Then** the row "Git repository" shows the sub-line "Not connected" and
  no chip. **When** it is opened, **Then** a paragraph says: "The drivers, architecture, ADRs, principles, architectural enablers,
  stories and diagrams are kept in a repository, so that code generation can use them. When you connect, everything that is already
  there is downloaded once from the base branch into this project. After that, Sync moves changes in both directions."
- [ ] **Given** the backend offers GitHub and GitLab, **Then** two options show, "GitHub" and "GitLab". None is selected, no field shows
  and Connect is disabled.
- [ ] **Given** the backend offers only GitHub, **Then** no choice is shown and the fields of GitHub show.
- [ ] **Given** the user chooses "GitHub", **Then** the fields are "GitHub API key" (a password field, placeholder "github_pat_..."),
  Repository (placeholder "owner/name"), Base branch ("main") and Folder in the repository ("bwyn"). **Given** the user chooses "GitLab",
  **Then** the fields are "GitLab API key" (placeholder "glpat-..."), Host (placeholder and default "https://gitlab.com"), Project
  (placeholder "group/project"), Base branch ("main") and Folder in the repository ("bwyn").
- [ ] **Given** a key was typed, **When** the user chooses the other option, **Then** the key field is empty, so that a key is never sent
  to a provider it does not belong to.
- [ ] **Given** the key field of GitHub, **Then** a hint says: "A fine-grained personal access token for the repository, with Contents and
  Pull requests both set to read and write. For a repository of an organization, create it with that organization as resource owner. It
  is sent to the BWYN backend, which checks it with GitHub and keeps it. The browser does not keep it."
- [ ] **Given** the key field of GitLab, **Then** a hint says: "A personal, project or group access token with the api scope, and the role
  Developer or higher on the project. It is sent to the BWYN backend, which checks it with GitLab and keeps it. The browser does not
  keep it."
- [ ] **Given** the form, **Then** Connect is disabled while Repository (or Project) is empty.

Checking the fields

- [ ] **Given** a GitHub repository written "acme/platform", "https://github.com/acme/platform" or "https://github.com/acme/platform.git/",
  with spaces around it, **Then** all are read as owner "acme" and name "platform". **Given** something else (for example "platform"),
  **When** Connect, **Then** "Write the repository as owner/name." shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** a GitLab project written "acme/platform", "acme/team/platform" (a subgroup) or "https://gitlab.com/acme/team/platform.git/",
  **Then** all are read as a project path. **Given** only one word, **Then** "Write the project as group/name, or
  group/subgroup/name." shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** a Host that is not an https address (for example "http://gitlab.acme.com" or "gitlab"), **Then** "The host looks wrong, for
  example https://gitlab.com." shows and nothing is sent. **Given** the project is an address on a host other than the Host field,
  **Then** "This address is not on <host>." shows.
- [ ] **Given** an empty key (or only spaces), **Then** "Paste the GitHub API key." (or "Paste the GitLab API key.") shows and nothing is
  sent. **Given** a key with spaces inside, or longer than 500 characters, **Then** "Paste the key without spaces." shows and nothing
  is kept.
- [ ] **Given** an empty branch, **Then** "main" is used. **Given** a folder with slashes at its ends, **Then** they are taken off, and an
  empty folder means the root of the repository ("(root)").
- [ ] **Given** a folder with ".." in it or with a character other than letters, digits, "_", ".", "/" and "-", **Then** "Invalid base
  folder." shows and nothing is kept.

Connecting

- [ ] **Given** valid fields, **When** the user presses Connect, **Then** the button reads "Connecting...", the backend checks the key with
  the provider (on that host, for GitLab), then the repository, then the base branch, and the card shows the chip "Connected" and the
  sub-line "acme/platform · main". The form is gone.
- [ ] **Given** the connected card, **Then** it shows: Provider ("GitHub" or "GitLab"), Repository (a link that opens it on the provider),
  the Host when it is not gitlab.com, Base branch and folder ("main · bwyn", or "main · (root)"), Last sync ("Not synced yet") and Signed
  in as (the key's user).
- [ ] **Given** the key cannot push (GitHub), or its role is below Developer (GitLab), **Then** an amber note says "The key may not be
  allowed to push to this repository, so uploads can fail."
- [ ] **Given** the provider refuses the key, **Then** "GitHub did not accept this API key." (or "GitLab did not accept this API key.")
  shows, the card stays "Not connected" and nothing is kept.
- [ ] **Given** the repository does not exist or the key cannot see it, **Then** the message the provider gave shows (for example "GitHub
  404: Not Found"), and nothing is kept. **Given** the provider answers 403, **Then** the message adds the advice: for GitHub, "Check the
  key on GitHub: its repository access must include this repository, Contents and Pull requests must both be "Read and write", and for
  an organization repository the key must be created with that organization as resource owner."; for GitLab, "Check the key on GitLab: it
  needs the api scope, and the role Developer or higher on the project."
- [ ] **Given** a branch that does not exist, **Then** 'The branch "x" was not found.' shows and nothing is kept.
- [ ] **Given** the provider cannot be reached, **Then** "GitHub could not be reached." (or "GitLab could not be reached at <host>.") shows,
  the card stays as it was, and Connect tries again.
- [ ] **Given** a project on a self-managed GitLab, **Then** the key is sent only to that host, and to no other.
- [ ] **Given** the same project later, **When** the provider no longer accepts the saved key (it was revoked), **Then** the card shows, in
  red, "<Provider> did not accept the saved key: <reason>".

The key stays on the backend

- [ ] **Given** Connect, **Then** the browser sends the key once, to the BWYN backend over its REST API. It never calls GitHub or GitLab,
  and the key is not in the bundle, in the browser storage or in any answer to the browser.
- [ ] **Given** the status of the connection is asked for, **Then** the answer has the provider, the host, the repository, the branch, the
  folder, the user and whether it is connected, and never the key.
- [ ] **Given** a refused key or a failed request, **Then** the key is not in the error message nor in the logs.
- [ ] **Given** two projects, **Then** each has its own provider, key and repository, and a request of one never uses the other's key.
- [ ] **Given** the connected project, **When** the page is reloaded, **Then** it is still connected, with the same fields.

Changing and removing

- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Change repository", **Then** the form of the same provider shows with the current
  repository (or project), branch and folder, and the key field is empty with "Leave empty to keep the current key". **When** the user
  saves with a new repository, **Then** everything is checked with the kept key, and the record of what was last synchronised is
  cleared, so that nothing is compared against another repository.
- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Change provider", **Then** the options show with the note "Connecting replaces the
  current connection (GitHub)." and a Cancel that keeps everything as it was.
- [ ] **Given** the user connects the other provider and the check passes, **Then** the card shows the new connection, and the old key and
  settings, and the record of the synchronisation, are deleted.
- [ ] **Given** the check of a changed repository or provider fails, **Then** the old connection is still there and works, and nothing of
  the attempt is kept.
- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Remove the key", **Then** the card says "Not connected", the key and the settings
  are deleted from the backend, and the record of the synchronisation is cleared.
- [ ] **Given** no connection, **Then** every Sync button in the app is disabled, and its hint is "Connect a Git repository in
  Integrations first". **Given** a connection (to either provider), **Then** they are enabled.

## Business rules and constraints

- There are two providers: **GitHub**, and **GitLab** (gitlab.com or a self-managed host). They are the only ones offered, and the backend
  lists them from its configuration. Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and the rest are not.
- An API key is the only credential. Signing in with an account, OAuth, SSH keys and deploy keys are not used. A key belongs to one
  provider and one host.
- A project has one connection at a time: one provider, one key, one repository, one base branch, one folder. Every project has its own.
- A GitLab project is a path of one or more groups and a name. BWYN accepts the path or the address of the project.
- The key is kept by the backend, never by the browser, and is never in any answer. How it is encrypted at rest is a decision for an ADR.
- "Connected" means the provider accepted the key, the repository is visible with it, and the base branch exists. A failed attempt never
  removes a working connection.
- The folder keeps BWYN's files apart from the rest of the repository. Everything BWYN reads and writes is inside it.
- The browser never calls the provider. It calls the BWYN backend, through one provider-neutral contract (the Reference).
- Words that name the provider (the key, the repository, the pull or merge request, the links) come from the provider, never written in
  the screens that use the connection.

## Out of scope

- Starting from what the repository has (story 2), and sending and receiving (stories 3 to 6).
- GitHub Enterprise Server (a GitHub on the team's own host), GitHub Apps, GitLab sign-in, and signing in with an account.
- Several providers at once for one project, mirroring a repository to the other provider, and moving a project's history from one to the
  other.
- More than one repository for a project, and one key shared by several projects.
- How the key is encrypted at rest.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Task 1. Connect with GitHub** (ships GitHub alone, with no choice shown)
  - Describe in the OpenAPI document the calls `providers`, and `connection` (put, get, delete) with the fields above, and no key in any
    answer.
  - Define in the backend one interface for a Git provider, and its first implementation for GitHub: check the key (the user), the
    repository (and whether the key can push) and the base branch, with the messages above, including the 403 advice.
  - Keep one connection per project: the key (never returned) and the repository settings, replaced only after a successful check.
  - Replace the dev server's one global token (and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` of `.env.spike`) with the key of each project.
  - Turn "Git (GitHub)" into the "Git repository" card: the GitHub fields and their checks, the connected view, "Change repository" and
    "Remove the key", with the providers read from the backend.
  - Make the Sync buttons read the connection of the project, with the hint "Connect a Git repository in Integrations first".
  - Test the GitHub provider against a fake GitHub server: a good key, a refused key, a missing repository, a 403, a missing branch, an
    unreachable server, and the key absent from every answer and every log line.
- [ ] **Task 2. Connect with GitLab** (adds the choice)
  - Add the host to the connection (`connection` put and get), and give `providers` the fields each provider needs.
  - Implement the GitLab provider: check the key (the user), the project (and the role) and the base branch on the given host, with the
    messages above (the Reference lists the calls).
  - Check the host (an https address) and the project path, and send the key only to that host.
  - Build the provider choice and the GitLab fields in the card, clear the key when the choice changes, and add "Change provider", with the
    old connection staying until the new one is checked.
  - Make the card, the dialogs and the notices take the provider's own words: the key, the project, the host, the link to the repository.
  - Run the tests of Task 1 against a fake GitLab server, with the same cases, and a project in a subgroup and a self-managed host.
